body.statement: Using the reverse-ancestral packing handle, determine the exact closed-form function \(Q_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)\) such that \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)=Q_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)\) for every \(s\ge d\), and prove matching full-oracle transcript lower bounds within \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{cf}}_{n,K,d}\).
body.justification: Cycle-free mixture ancestry removes the feedback-set penalty while retaining emergent edges, isolating the pure count cost of parent blocking.
body.gap: The anchor proves optimal maximum intervention size and a headwise quadratic-count algorithm, not an exact adaptive count law.
body.consumer: The result gives the smallest experiment count for mixtures whose component ancestries admit a common acyclic processing order.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact closed form of \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)\) throughout \(s\ge d\).
obligation.obstruction: Reverse ancestral processing proves correctness at panel size \(d\), but its headwise candidate tests can overlap in transcript-dependent ways. The current legal lower alternatives do not certify that the resulting quadratic count, or any proposed batching improvement, is optimal.
obligation.attempted: Certified-parent blocking yields a policy with at most \(n+n(n-1)\) queries, and empty-baseline single-edge alternatives give an antichain-type lower constraint. For \(d>1\), these constraints do not force the simultaneous parent blockers used by the upper policy.
obligation.partial_result: Feasibility is exactly \(s\ge d\); a finite policy uses at most \(n+n(n-1)\) queries; and the indegree-one singleton slice is exactly \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,1,1)=n\).
